newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes lower as Egypt buys French wheat.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes lower as Egypt buys French wheat.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed lower and new contract lows were set in the March and May with news over the weekend that Egypt bought French rather than U.S. wheat, pulling values down, traders said.
"Egypt buying wheat from France didn't help, that's bearish too..the increased global competition," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.
The Egyptian state's main grain buyer said Sunday Egypt bought 450,000 tonnes of wheat from France. U.S. exporters said Egypt bought the wheat at $10 to $15 per tonne below U.S. prices.
The new contract low for March is $4.09 per bushel, below the previous low of $4.20 set Friday. The new low for May is $3.95 per bushel, below the previous low of $4.04 also set Friday.
"It was a little disappointing in wheat with Egypt taking wheat out of France," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co.
Funds and commercials sold wheat. Cargill Inc sold 2.5 million bushels of December as did LIT America and R.J. O'Brien, they said.
Wheat closed one to 8-3/4 cents per bushel lower, with September down 5-3/4 at $4.23-1/4.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 18,000 contracts, down slightly from 18,141 Friday, according to the CBOT.

In wheat options LIT America sold 300 December $4.40 calls at 7-1/2 cents, Merrill Lynch Futures bought 200 December $4.60 puts at 48 cents and Refco Inc bought 200 December $4.40 calls at 7-1/2 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 7,500 contracts, up from 5,808 Friday.
